name: Lincoln Electric Holdings, Inc.
moat_justification: Global #1 arc-welding franchise: ROIC 22.5-28.2% over the last five fiscal years (17.6% even in the 2020 trough) and gross margin expanded 32.8% to 36.2%, with proven pricing power (Q2 2026 organic +10.1% was +7.7pp price). Tempered by capable scaled rivals (ESAB, ITW/Miller), partly commoditized consumables, and hard industrial cyclicality.
fragility_flags: STALE_FY: latest fiscal year ended 10 months ago — check TTM/quarterly OE and consider --base-oe-ps override
one_liner: High-quality welding franchise, moat 7/10 with 22-28% ROIC — but at $262.10 it cannot clear 15% in any scenario (weighted IRR 7.4%, IV@15% $96.85); it clears the 15% hurdle only at ~$97.
moat_for: ROIC 22.5-28.2% across the last five fiscal years, 17.6% in the 2020 trough (fundamentals.json roic_proxy)
Gross margin expanded from 32.8% (2020) to 36.2% (2025) — demonstrated pricing power
Global #1 share in arc welding; brand, distribution and application engineering specify welds into fabricator processes
Consumables pull-through on the installed equipment base plus a growing automation/robotics offering
Q2 2026 price realization +7.7pp of +10.1% organic growth; FY2026 guidance raised to low-double-digit sales growth
moat_against: ESAB and ITW (Miller Electric) are large, well-resourced rivals across the same portfolio
Electrodes and consumables face regional and private-label price competition; no network effects
Industrial-capex cyclicality: nine straight quarters of volume decline before the Q2 2026 inflection; International/Europe still weak
Steel and specialty-metal input costs plus tariff/trade exposure compress margins in adverse years
